exam: Explain the pathophysiology of ovarian torsion and why it causes acute pain.
List the imaging findings that support the diagnosis and their limitations.
Describe the surgical management steps and the rationale for ovarian preservation.
ai.subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
ai.summary: Ovarian torsion is the twisting of the ovary (often with the fallopian tube) causing vascular compromise. Prompt recognition and surgery are essential to preserve ovarian function and prevent necrosis.

b: Most often triggered by a cyst >5 cm
Can be intermittent, causing recurrent pain
Occurs in both sides, right side slightly more common
sections.p: A sudden rotation of the ovary around its ligamentous supports cuts off arterial inflow and venous outflow, leading to ischemia. It can occur at any age but is most common in reproductive‑age women with ovarian cysts or masses.

b: Ischemia begins within minutes; irreversible damage after ~24 h
Detorsion is attempted before oophorectomy when feasible
Underlying mass often benign but malignancy must be excluded
sections.p: The torsion angle, duration of ischemia, and underlying lesion determine severity. Early detorsion may restore perfusion; prolonged torsion leads to necrosis and loss of ovarian tissue.

b: Pain may be intermittent if torsion partially resolves
Nausea/vomiting reflect peritoneal irritation
Absence of fever helps differentiate from PID
sections.p: Patients present with acute unilateral lower‑abdomen pain, often with nausea and vomiting. Physical exam may show a tender adnexal mass and absent ovarian blood flow on Doppler.
Imaging and labs guide diagnosis but should not delay surgery if clinical suspicion is high.

t.b: Absent or markedly reduced flow suggests torsion; normal flow does not rule it out
Positive test prompts consideration of ectopic pregnancy; negative supports torsion
Mild leukocytosis is common; marked elevation suggests alternative diagnosis

b: If laparoscopy unavailable, perform open laparotomy
Administer IV fluids and analgesia while awaiting OR
Give broad‑spectrum antibiotics only if infection suspected
sections.p: Immediate surgical detorsion (laparoscopy preferred) is the definitive treatment. Preserve the ovary when viable; remove necrotic tissue if necessary.
